assumptions.text: On a Screening Service outage (when ScreeningService.screen raises ScreeningUnavailableError), the quote must be refused with status "refused_screening" and otherwise follow the refused-screening path (stored draft retained, no price, refusal notice attempt, fire-and-forget). This adopts the architectural assistant note as resolving OD-1.

If ScreeningService.screen returns a non-integer risk_index, it is still treated as a numeric value and compared to the DT-S thresholds without additional type validation, because the spec only normatively constrains DT-V input fields from the request.

If QuoteStore.update_quote fails (raises StoreUnavailableError or any other exception), the error is allowed to propagate; the specification does not define behaviour for update failures, only for the initial draft storage failure.
If TariffEngine.price raises an exception other than StoreUnavailableError, it is allowed to propagate; the documents do not define a pricing-error status or fallback behaviour.
If NotificationService methods raise any exception, it is swallowed so that the response and stored outcome remain unchanged, implementing the fire-and-forget rule.

claims.text: DT-V defines request validity: all four fields must be present and within specific numeric bounds; invalid requests are rejected immediately with status "rejected: invalid_request" and no draft storage, screening, pricing, or notification happens.
On storage failure when storing the draft quote, the system must return status "error: store_unavailable" and must not call screening, pricing, or notification.

The flow order is: validate (DT-V), store draft, request risk index, apply screening decision (DT-S) and update stored quote, price (DT-P) only on priced rows, notify only on notified rows, then return response.

DT-S defines three bands: accept (risk_index <= 41) → priced and notified with status "quoted"; review (42 <= risk_index <= 66) → no price, no notification, status "review_hold"; refuse (risk_index >= 67) → no price, notified with refusal notice, status "refused_screening".
Notification is fire-and-forget: any delivery failure never changes the stored quote or the response.

DT-P defines pricing: base = 0.87 * weight_kg + 1.13 * distance_km; if weight_kg > 1244 add 316.00 flat; if distance_km >= 4912 multiply running total by 1.19 after P2; then price is round(result, 2).

The API response must always include a status that is exactly one of: "quoted", "review_hold", "refused_screening", "rejected: invalid_request", "error: store_unavailable"; quote_id is present whenever a draft was stored; price is present exactly on the priced rows of DT-S.
On review-band outcomes, no price is computed and no notification is sent; on refused outcomes, pricing never runs and a refusal notice is sent.
Request validation bounds in DT-V are mirrored in the OpenAPI schema: shipper_id is a non-empty string; weight_kg 3-19400; distance_km 25-7150; declared_value 50-83000.
